title: Photon Bounce: On Your Own
subject: earth science
instructions: Answer on your own, even though you played with your group. ppm means parts per million. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.skill: I can read a graph of measurements
questions.prompt: Real Measurements: NOAA measures carbon dioxide (CO₂) in the air on Mauna Loa, Hawaii. Circle the 1960 and 2020 points. About how many ppm did CO₂ rise between them?

diagram.description: A line graph of CO₂ (ppm, 300 to 440) by year (1960 to 2030), with dots at 1960 (317), 1970 (326), 1980 (339), 1990 (354), 2000 (370), 2010 (390), 2020 (414), and 2025 (427). Small print: 'Data: NOAA, Mauna Loa annual means'.

shapes.text: Data: NOAA, Mauna Loa annual means

checklist.item: The 1960 point (about 317 ppm) and the 2020 point (about 414 ppm) are circled.

questions.notes: 414.21 − 316.91 = 97.3 ppm. Values read off the graph from 95 to 100 are right. Look for 414 or 317 (a reading, not the rise).

questions.skill: I can explain the greenhouse effect
questions.prompt: Absorb What? In the game, what did the air layers absorb?

options.text: Sunlight coming down from the Sun
options.why: Sunlight passed straight through to the ground.

options.text: Infrared given off by the warm ground
options.why: Yes: CO₂ absorbs infrared, not sunlight.

options.text: Cold air coming down from space
options.why: Only sunlight and infrared moved in the game.

questions.skill: I can explain the greenhouse effect
questions.prompt: More CO₂: When the game switched from low to high CO₂, what happened?

options.text: More infrared escaped to space right away.
options.why: More was absorbed on the way up.

options.text: More infrared came back down to the ground.
options.why: Yes: more absorbed, half sent back down.
Compare your low and high CO₂ rounds.

questions.skill: I can explain the greenhouse effect
questions.prompt: Without It: With no greenhouse gases at all, Earth's average surface temperature would be about −18 °C instead of about 15 °C. Use the game to explain why.

rubric.criterion: Absorb: says gases in the air absorb infrared given off by the ground (not sunlight).
Back down: says the gases give the energy off again, some of it back down to the ground.
Without: says with none, all the infrared escapes, so the ground gets less energy and is colder.
